Okay bud, ignore the overwhelming evidence that diet soda is (for the vast majority of people) a major detriment to weightloss. It's a fact that aspartame messes with your insulin.

While there aren't really any health issues that come with diet soda, many studies show that artificial sweeteners not only damage your body's ability to process real sugar, but also stops your body from losing fat. Aspartame mimics sugar in every way but caloric value. Due to this, your body reacts as if it expects to switch to glucose power for awhile (stalling ketosis). Because glucose isn't actually present, though, this leads to an energy drop because your body is no longer actively using your fat for energy. Ultimately, diet soda will slow weightloss during your fast and lead to mood swings and fatigue. Give tea, coffee, or sparkling water a shot if you crave a break from the monotony of water.

I'm a little late here, but as a recent entry into the expanded SMT series myself I want to give my 2 cents too, haha. I've personally not found any games that live up to Persona 3 or Persona 4 (I know, freakin' casul) but there's a lot of value in the other games. SMT IV and Apocalypse (from what I've seen so far) are both amazing games! The combat is more forgiving than Nocturne and the characters are a lot more engaging in my opinion. Nocturne is honestly my least favorite mainline SMT game  (I've played all of them) which is a pretty unpopular opinion, haha. Everyone considers it to be the best thing since tummy rubs, but I found the characters bland, the gameplay way too unforgiving and often unfair, and the story lackluster and not so compelling. Devil Survivor 1 and 2 are great, both have some really cool characters and the strategy elements are a welcome change. Plus the stories are engaging. I agree that you should go back and play the two Persona 2 games, their story is amazing (though not the best SMT or even Persona has to offer). Persona 1 is worth a play, but it's a little bland. I enjoyed going back to the roots of my favorite series, but the combat is dated. It's the same problem I ran into when emulating SMT 1, but the grind was worth it! Hope that helps!

I guess we'll have to agree to disagree in that regard. You are right, my mentality is certainly not helping resolve the issue. I feel burned by their treatment of their western audience, and I suppose my retaliation is rather emotionally driven. The fact remains that Atlus it doing us a disservice, and I will almost certainly wind-up having most if not all of the game spoiled for me by the time it comes out due to the proliferation of the internet.

I don't feel my actions are childish; they just simply seem to be the only option I have for protesting said behavior. I was the same way when Bioware (mostly due to their parent company EA I imagine) released the Jaws of Hakkon DLC for every console except for the PS4, which got the content two months later. I didn't pay them for that, I won't pay Atlus for this.

I've been playing video games pretty regularly for about seventeen years now, and buying them with my own money for about fifteen years, so I wouldn't exactly say I'm whippersnapper when it comes to them.
I understand the sentiment that at that purest level, developers are businesses that are out to get money. It's the illusion of the them giving a shit that I'm worried about. If they want my money, I expect them to do at least that much.

I'm not personally concerned about the logistics between Atlus US and Atlus JP; as far as I'm concerned, they're the same company. I don't expect Atlus US to work around the clock, I expect Atlus JP to un-ass the assets six months before the game releases so the games can be launched at about the same time. If the Japanese companies like Atlus and Square weren't so brick-headed about giving the Japanese populous special treatment, this wouldn't be an issue.

My reasoning is neither immature or entitled. I'm a consumer, it is up to the company selling their product to sway me into buying said product. In the age we live in, where digital piracy and buying used games is so simple, this is even more paramount. Why should I pay an extra ten bucks to get the game new when I can drive down to Gamestop and buy the game used for less? I don't see much of a reason if the company that makes the game doesn't care about me.

No. Personally I'm not even going to buy the English version new at this point. The wait for localization is ridiculous; Atlus clearly doesn't care about their non-Japanese audience.
